source.dataset: NASA GEOS Composition Forecasting system (GEOS-CF), July-August 2024

frames.label: Fine particles (PM2.5)
frames.alt: World map of fine particles, PM2.5, summer 2024: cream where the air is clean, orange to dark brown where smoke and dust are thick, over Canada, Siberia, the Sahara and Central Africa.

frames.label: Carbon monoxide
frames.alt: World map of carbon monoxide, summer 2024: pale yellow where it is low, red where it is high, over the Canadian and Siberian fires and the burning season in Central Africa.

frames.label: Nitrogen oxides
frames.alt: World map of nitrogen oxides, summer 2024: black and white where there is almost none, dark green over industry and traffic in eastern China, India, Europe and the United States.

frames.label: Ozone
frames.alt: World map of surface ozone, summer 2024: grey where it is low, deep purple where it is high, over the Mediterranean, the Middle East, China and North America.

legend.summary: Four kinds of air pollution from NASA's GEOS-CF model, July and August 2024, a summer of huge wildfires in Canada: fine particles, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides and ozone. A scan line crosses the world once for each, west to east.
legend.method: Places in the north sound higher and in your left ear; places in the south lower and in your right. Clean air is a quiet, open drone. Where the air is dirty, notes ring and the drone turns harsh and sour, so the worst air sounds the most uneasy.

items.meaning: Places where this pollutant is thick, played as the scan line crosses them. Louder = thicker.
All the pollution under the scan line. It grows rough and sour where the air is worst.

legend.caveat: Levels are read from the colours of NASA's movie, so they are relative: 0 is the clean end of NASA's colour scale for that pollutant, 100 the dirty end. Each pollutant has its own scale, so compare places, not pollutants.
